# 1 Clement Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_018_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 18

**18:1** And what do we say about David? He received God's highest attestation — God himself said: "I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, anointed with my everlasting mercy." [Ps 89:20; 1 Sam 13:14]

**18:2** And yet this same David says to God: "God, have mercy on me in your great love. In your overflowing compassion, wipe away my sin.

**18:3** Wash me clean from my guilt; purify me from my wrongdoing. I know what I've done; I can't get away from it.

**18:4** I've sinned against you and you alone — done what you call wrong. So when you pass judgment, you will be right, and no one can dispute your verdict.

**18:5** I've been guilty since before I was born — a sinner from my mother's womb.

**18:6** But you prize honesty; you have opened up to me the hidden depths of your wisdom.

**18:7** Purify me with hyssop and I'll be clean. Wash me and I'll be whiter than snow.

**18:8** Let me hear the sounds of joy and celebration — let the bones you've crushed begin to dance.

**18:9** Look away from my sins; erase every record of my wrongdoing.

**18:10** Create in me a pure heart, O God. Give me a new, steadfast spirit.

**18:11** Don't banish me from your presence. Don't take your Holy Spirit from me.

**18:12** Give me back the joy of being rescued by you. Keep me going with a willing, generous spirit.

**18:13** Then I will teach wrongdoers your ways, and sinners will return to you.

**18:14** Free me from guilt for bloodshed, O God — my rescuing God — and I will sing out loud about your justice.

**18:15** Lord, open my mouth, and I will praise you.

**18:16** You don't want sacrifices — I would give them if you did. Burnt offerings don't satisfy you.

**18:17** What you want is a broken spirit. A broken and crushed heart — that, O God, you will never reject." [Ps 51:1-17]

---

*PNEUMA renders Psalm 51 with contemporary emotional directness.*
